name: Gilt market
summary: 10-year gilt yield above 5.3% on 13 Nov, highest since late October; an 11 Nov auction drew 3.94x cover
state: The 10-year gilt yield rose above 5.3% on 13 Nov, its highest since late October, from about 5.15% on 6 Nov, after the Bank of England's first rate rise in over three years and growing bets on further rises (Trading Economics). That is well inside the 40bp monthly move line. The DMO's 11 Nov sale of £1bn of 2028 gilts drew 3.94 times cover, so auctions remain orderly (DMO). Long-dated yields near multi-decade highs keep Watch.
for_you: Higher gilt yields tend to feed through to fixed mortgage and loan pricing over the following weeks, and to annuity rates. The Bank of England publishes its rate decisions and market notices on its website.
rubric_hit: 30y gilt near multi-decade highs = Watch; 10y monthly move < 40bp and 11 Nov auction 3.94x cover

sources.title: Trading Economics — UK Bond Yields Edge Up (page's news stream shows 10-year above 5.3% on 13 Nov)

why: Gilt yields set UK mortgage rates and the government's borrowing costs; the 2022 LDI crisis showed how fast it can break.
drivers: Fiscal credibility, BoE policy, inflation, global bond moves, pension-fund flows.

rubric.alert: BoE intervention, or 10y moved > 75bp in a month.
rubric.watch: 30y gilt at multi-decade highs, or 10y moved 40–75bp in a month, or a weak auction.
rubric.normal: 10y gilt moved < 40bp in a month and auctions orderly.
